pull.meaning: downloads new commits from the remote and merges them into your branch.
pull.resultZero: {remote} had nothing new — you're already up to date.
steps: reached out to {remote}
found {n} new commit{s} you didn't have yet
merged them into {branch}
stepsZero: it has nothing you don't already have
pull.authError: you're not logged in to pull from this remote.
pull.networkError: couldn't reach {remote} — check your network or VPN connection.

push.meaning: uploads your commits so the remote matches your branch.
push.resultZero: nothing to push — {remote} already matches your branch.
steps: checked what {remote} already has
sent it the {n} commit{s} it was missing
{remote} now matches {branch}
stepsZero: it already matches your branch — nothing to send
push.authError: you're not logged in to push to this remote.
push.networkError: couldn't reach {remote} — check your network or VPN connection.

stash.meaning: sets uncommitted changes aside so your working directory is clean.
stash.result: saved {n} changed file{s} — bring them back with stash pop.
stash.resultZero: nothing to save — no changed files.
steps: took every tracked change out of your working directory
saved {n} file{s} as a stash entry
your working directory is clean now
stepsZero: nothing tracked was changed — there was nothing to set aside

applyStash.meaning: brings "{target}" back into your working directory, keeping the stash entry.
applyStash.result: applied "{target}" — it's still in your stash list too.
steps: took the stashed changes
reapplied them to your working directory
kept the stash entry in case you need it again

popStash.meaning: brings "{target}" back into your working directory and removes the stash entry.
popStash.result: popped "{target}" — it's back in your working directory.
steps: took the stashed changes
reapplied them to your working directory
removed the stash entry since it's been restored

dropStash.meaning: deletes "{target}" for good — the changes it held are gone.
steps: found the stash entry
deleted it
the changes it held can't be brought back

commit.meaning: saves your staged changes as a new point in your branch's history.
steps: packaged the {n} file{s} you staged
created a new commit on {branch}
{branch}'s tip moved forward to it

switchBranch.meaning: points your working directory at a different branch.
steps: checked your working directory was safe to switch
moved HEAD to {branch}
your files now match {branch}'s last commit

createBranch.meaning: creates a new branch starting from {from}, and switches to it.
steps: created a new branch pointer at {from}
switched your working directory to it
{branch} points at the same commit as {from} for now — they'll diverge once you commit

revert.meaning: undoes commits by adding a new commit that reverses them — nothing is deleted from history.
steps: found the {n} commit{s} after {target}
created new commit{s} that undo exactly their changes
nothing was deleted — {target} and everything after it still exist in history
revert.confirmText: this adds new commit{s} that undo the {n} commit{s} after {target} — none of them are deleted, and this is safe even if they've been pushed. continue?
revert.conflictPaused: git paused the revert here — {files} conflict. resolve them in your editor or terminal, then come back and continue.

reset.meaning: moves {branch} back to {target}. what happens to the commits' changes depends on the mode you pick.
reset.soft: moved {branch} back to {target} — your changes from the {n} commit{s} stay staged, ready to commit again.
reset.mixed: moved {branch} back to {target} — your changes from the {n} commit{s} stay, but unstaged.
reset.hard: moved {branch} back to {target} and discarded the {n} commit{s} and their changes.
reset.modeSoft: keeps the changes from the commits you're moving past — staged, ready to commit again.
reset.modeMixed: keeps the changes from the commits you're moving past — but unstaged, like you never committed them.
reset.modeHard: throws away the changes from the commits you're moving past. this can't be undone through the app.
reset.alreadyPushedWarning: some of these commits are already on your remote. resetting past them will diverge your branch from the shared history. continue?
reset.confirmDiscard: this will permanently discard {n} commit{s} and their changes. continue?

undo.meaning: reverses your last action so things are back to how they were.
steps: found exactly what your last action changed
reversed it
nothing else was touched

merge.resultZero: {target} was already merged into {branch} — nothing to do.
steps: checked how {branch} and {target} relate
combined {target}'s {n} commit{s} into {branch}
{branch} now has a new merge commit joining both histories
stepsFastForward: {branch} had no commits of its own since diverging, so it just moved forward
no new merge commit was needed
merge.fastForward: this will fast-forward {branch} to include {target}'s {n} commits.
merge.clean: this will merge {target} into {branch}, {n} commits, no conflicts.
merge.wouldConflict: this will merge {target} into {branch}, but {files} conflict — you'll need to resolve them.
merge.conflictPaused: git paused the merge here — {files} conflict. resolve them in your editor or terminal, then come back and continue.

rebase.meaning: replays {branch}'s commits one at a time on top of {target}, giving each one a new commit hash.
steps: found the {n} commit{s} unique to {branch}
replayed each one on top of {target}, one at a time
{branch} now points at the last replayed commit
rebase.alreadyPushedWarning: some of these commits are already on your remote. rebasing rewrites their history, which can cause real problems for anyone who's already pulled them. continue?
rebase.plan: this will replay {n} commits from {branch} onto {target}, one at a time, giving them new commit hashes.
rebase.conflictPaused: git paused the rebase on commit {current} of {total} — {files} conflict. resolve them in your editor or terminal, then come back and continue.
